analysis:
This batch is test-only. The changes are GLM5NextProviderLoopTests.swift head 70-77 and 194-220, the new VerifiedWeightHashStoreTests.swift (1-104), and StartupPreloadTests.swift head 298-315. Together they imply new production behavior (VerifiedWeightHashStore, setLoadWeightHasherForTesting, liveModelHashForTesting, weightsVerifiedByManagedLoad, StartupPreloader onFailure); that production source is not in this batch.

Security-relevant implications (T-012, T-027, A-004, T-041 weightHash binding):
1. A GLM managed load now publishes the manifest aggregateSHA256 as the live registration hash without a separate WeightHasher read (GLM test 212-213). The digest is persisted to a records file keyed by modelID plus file identities (214-216).
2. Later starts may reuse a recorded hash while the file identities match, avoiding a rehash. The tests assert that rewrite (with restored mtime), append and added files all invalidate the record, relying on ctime/inode (VerifiedWeightHashStoreTests 56-82).
3. The records file mode is 0600 (53). Corrupt or foreign-schema state is ignored (84-95).
4. Only modelType glm5_next is treated as verified by its managed load (97-103).

Questions the integration pass must check against production source:
(a) The managed load must actually SHA-256 the bytes it maps, not just trust the revision receipt. Otherwise the reported weightHash is self-attested from the manifest, and operator weight substitution (T-012) is undetected.
(b) FileIdentity must include inode, device, ctime and size for every snapshot file, including symlink targets. ctime is operator-resettable only with root or clock changes; a same-UID operator is already ADV-001 and weight hashes are self-reported anyway, so this is not a new trust grant.
(c) The records file location and permissions, and whether any attacker-writable record could inject a hash. This matters little because the operator controls the provider.
(d) The weightHash consumed by SSD prefix-cache binding (T-041) must come from the same verified value.
(e) The StartupPreloader onFailure hook passes error.localizedDescription. Check where it is sent (telemetry?) and that it contains no prompt data. Preload errors are model-load errors, so the risk is low.

No regression is identified in the test code itself.
